messages:
Anna (arch): Quick check-in on propagating tenant/principal context across Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private adapters. I sketched three approaches below and a minimal acceptance checklist. Looking for concerns and missing tradeoffs before I formalize an RFC.

Anna (arch): Context: Incoming hosted requests carry an auth token and tenant metadata. When we hand off to an adapter (dedicated pool or private sidecar) we must ensure downstream has a verifiable tenant/principal for billing, policy, and audit without exposing long-lived secrets or requiring customers to share keys.

Anna (arch): Approach A — Transparent forward: include original bearer in X-Redwood-Forwarded-Auth header (opaque to transit). Adapter validates with control plane or cache.
  - Good: minimal infra change, adapters treat token as source-of-truth.
  - Bad: spreads customer bearer tokens across network zones; unacceptable for some enterprise/legal customers.

Anna (arch): Approach B — Short-lived delegated creds (broker): Hosted calls token-broker to exchange inbound token for an adapter-scoped delegation token. Broker returns short TTL JWT with audience=adapter-instance and tenant assertion. Adapter uses it to reconstruct principal.
  - Good: reduces blast radius, supports audience restriction and KMS signing.
  - Bad: requires broker availability and increases cold-path latency.

Anna (arch): Approach C — Mutual identity + manifest (sidecar/offline): use mTLS identities and signed tenant binding manifests for private/air-gapped deployments; manifests are operator-provisioned and map local service identity -> tenant set.
  - Good: no customer tokens transmitted, workable offline.
  - Bad: operational complexity for rotation and for hosted shared pools.

Suman: For air-gapped/private: prefer the manifest route. Need clear manifest format and rotation story. Operator timeouts and rollbacks are important.

AJ: Emphatic: forwarding raw tokens will be rejected by some legal teams. Delegated broker should be default for public tenants.

Marco: Performance note: broker exchange adds a hop on the first request per adapter/tenant. Suggest prefetching delegated creds when routing decision is known (prefetch top-N tenants per pool) + local caching with telemetry on cached_miss_count.

Olivia: Logs requirement: adapters must emit canonical X-Redwood-Tenant and X-Redwood-Principal after successful validation. These must be scrubbed/redacted in public traces. Provide an opt-in hashed-principal mode (per-day salt) for privacy-preserving audit exports.

Anna (arch): Proposed minimal acceptance criteria for RFC:
  - Correctness: tenant and principal available for billing, policy, and audit in all hosting modes.
  - Security: no long-lived customer secrets stored in adapters; delegated tokens TTL <= 300s by default.
  - Availability: broker failures degrade gracefully (use cache/soft-fail) with observability (metrics and alerting).
  - Backcompat: adapters accept legacy X-Redwood-Forwarded-Auth for a transition window but log deprecation.
  - Offline: manifest format + rotation method for Private must be defined.

Suman: Rotation question: who signs manifests? Customer KMS or Redwood? For on-prem customers we must allow customer-signed manifests; for Dedicated we'll accept Redwood-signed operator manifests.

Anna (arch): Yes. Manifest signature must be verifiable by adapter via a trusted root local to that deployment. Add fields: version, issued_at, expires_at, binding_list, signature_alg, signer_id.

Marco: Ops hazard: if adapter sees invalid/expired manifest and broker unreachable, we should prefer cached tenant mappings with a short grace window (e.g., 10m) rather than immediate reject. Must count the incidents.

AJ: Also recommend delegation tokens bind to adapter-instance-id so they can't be replayed on other machines. Broker should include adapter instance in aud claim.

Olivia: Add requirement: scrub headers with sensitive tokens from panic logs and stack traces. Add unit test for stack dump redaction in adapter library.

Anna (arch): Example exchange flow (sketch):
POST /v1/token-broker/exchange
Auth: Bearer <hosted-token>
Body: {"adapter_audience":"adapter:dedicated:pool-7:instance-42","ttl":300}
-> 200 {"delegation":"eyJhbGci...","tenant_id":"acme-corp","principal":"alice@acme.com"}
Adapter validates signature, aud, and ttl and then emits X-Redwood-Tenant and X-Redwood-Principal locally.

Suman: For the manifest API: propose a local endpoint on adapter /v1/operator/manifest and an operator client that pushes signed manifests. Rotation policy configurable; default manifest check interval: 24h.

Marco: I'll prototype a lightweight broker shim + adapter validation lib with caching and prefetch hooks. Will include metrics: broker_exchange_latency, broker_exchange_errors, manifest_invalid_count, cached_lookup_hits.

Anna (arch): Next steps: Marco to prototype; Suman + Olivia to draft manifest schema and rotation API; AJ to collect legal constraints to lock defaults; I'll produce RFC draft from notes and the checklist and circulate early next week.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-01-15T09:22:10Z started by Marco  auth-broker-proto -> staging

Olivia: One last ask: include a privacy mode where principal values are hashed with a daily salt before being persisted in any external telemetry pipeline.

Anna (arch): Noted. Thanks everyone 9 :thumbsup:
